title: Normalized scalar witness and its shift square
statement: In the original geometric setup, there exists gamma satisfying the exact scalar-limit factorization; for every integral finite-Tor constructible M and integer r, M[r] is again integral finite-Tor constructible and gamma obeys its specified canonical shift equation. This is the gamma part of the final witness clause of the original theorem, with definitions [def-pur-compact-support-scalar-limit-maps] and shifts [def-pur-compact-support-scalar-shift-structures]. The strict-arrow and scalarLimitArrow shift squares of that clause follow from the strict scalar mate shift and scalar limit constraint shift lemmas and are not restated; nor are the original-site or diagram-site constituent CommShift clauses, normalization uniqueness or individual limit-constraint clauses.

source.place: Tags 05SU, 06YU, 07A6, 0B56, 0941, 099I, 099L; retained canonical scalar-shift argument of lem-pur-compact-support-scalar-shift-normalization.

proof.text:
obtain gamma and its exact factorization and completeness conclusions
from compactSupportScalarLimitReduction. Integral triangulated closure
(lem-pur-integral-ctf-shift-closure) supplies membership of each M[r]. The
scalarLimitArrow square is the last clause of scalarLimitConstraintShift.
Conjugate scalarLimitArrow by scalarCompletion and the support/limit
isomorphisms; their canonical shift squares (scalarLimitConstraintShift) produce
a shift-compatible beta on constant restrictions. The exact factorization gives
restriction(gamma)=beta by cancellation. Both support objects are complete.
Finite-free scalar extension preserves completeness by finite sums, and shifts
preserve completeness. The normalized constant/completed equivalence is fully
faithful on these objects. Restrict the gamma equation, use naturality of the
restriction shift, and substitute the two factorization equations at M and M[r].
The result is beta's shift square, so faithfulness proves it. This works for all
integer shifts, including zero and negative shifts; positive e is used only for
inverse arithmetic restriction.
